title: The long first flight to Australia with Red Norvo's trio
summary: In 1952 the slow little plane stopped at Fiji. Red Norvo brought a bass and guitar player; the guitarist later died in a fire, which Norvo's wife wrote to tell her.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe

blocks.x: Well anyway, of course naturally Red was very happy to have a good singer with him because he was used to having a good singer with him. Well had Red ever gone over there before?
This was in . . .
This was way back in 1952.
Yeah, as I said, that was in '52.
You know, they didn't have these fast planes and things. And I said, I wish I could get off of this plane. Honey, I'm telling you, that old plane, a little plane, you know?
Well it must have been a very long trip.
It was.
Did Red calm you down?
I just went to sleep. Then when we got to Fiji Island, then you'd get off and have all that

What did they feed you?
Oh, everything. Let me see. I don't know. I don't remember. But it sure was good.
And that made you feel better. But you didn't have - nobody else was out there with you. You and Red were appearing with groups that were there, weren't you?
No, Red had his bass and drummer.
Oh, he did?
Not drum; bass and guitar.
Oh, did he? Who, do you remember?
I'll remember it the next day. And this other boy got burned up in the place and that's when he wrote and told me about it, the guitar player.
Really? The bass player?
The guitar player got burned up.
Oh, and Red wrote you about it?
Red's wife.
Oh, Eve wrote you. I see.
But it was in all the papers.
